chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAlī عليه السلام said: No salat (prayer) is valid if the nose does not touch what the forehead touches.

So this narration is to be understood as indicating a type of dislike rather than obligation, because the obligation is sajdah upon the forehead, while pressing the nose to the ground is sunnah (prophetic tradition), as we have explained. And what we have said is further confirmed.

key_terms.الرِّوَايَةُ: the narration/report being interpreted by the author
key_terms.السُّجُودُ: sajdah, the act of prostration in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْأَنْفُ: the nose, whose contact in sajdah is mentioned in the narration
key_terms.الْجَبِينُ: the forehead area mentioned as the point of contact in prostration
key_terms.الْفَرْضِ: obligation, the binding requirement in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislike or reprehensibility, indicating non-obligatory disapproval
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: sunnah (prophetic tradition), indicating a recommended practice rather than an obligation
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is being discussed

ai.seo_question: Is touching the nose to the ground during sajdah obligatory in salat (prayer) or sunnah?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling of sajdah in salat (prayer), specifically whether the nose must touch the place of prostration along with the forehead. It explains that the obligation pertains to prostrating on the forehead, while placing the nose is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), so the report is interpreted as indicating karahah rather than invalidity.
